messages.text: We already get food stamps. Can my 3 year old also get WIC?

Yes, your 3-year-old will probably be able to get WIC. Getting food assistance (SNAP) helps a lot.

**What to do next**
1. Call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942), or contact your local county health department WIC clinic. You can find clinics at [tn.gov/health/wic.html](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).
2. Ask for a WIC appointment for your child.
3. Bring proof that your household gets food assistance (SNAP). A recent approval letter works. Ask the clinic what else to bring.

**Why it looks likely**
- WIC serves children until their 5th birthday, and your child is 3. Tennessee residents are eligible.
- WIC normally has an income limit of 185% of the poverty level. For example, a family of 3 can earn up to $50,542 a year before taxes. These limits run from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
- People who show proof that they get SNAP, Families First, or TennCare are automatically income-eligible.

(Source: [Tennessee Department of Health WIC page](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html))

**Things to know**
- **Health check:** WIC also needs a nutrition or health check. The clinic does this at the visit. It's usually quick.
- **Who is covered:** One local source says the SNAP proof can come from anyone in your household. Another suggests it may need to be the child or the person applying. Ask the clinic which applies to you. If it's a problem, you could still qualify on income.
- **Other family members:** If anyone in your home is pregnant, breastfeeding, or has a baby under 1, they may be able to get WIC too.

This is only a first look. The WIC clinic makes the final decision, and I can't promise an outcome. For free local help, you can also call 211.

Do you have a baby under 1, or is anyone in your home pregnant? I can check if they might get WIC too.

Sources:
- [Tennessee Department of Health: WIC](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html)
No, nobody's pregnant and we don't have a baby under 1. It's just me, my husband, and our son.

Thanks. That makes it simple. WIC is only for your 3-year-old in your case. You and your husband wouldn't be covered, because WIC serves pregnant or postpartum women, babies, and children under 5.

**What to do now**
1. Call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942), or contact your county health department's WIC clinic. You can find clinics at [tn.gov/health/wic.html](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).
2. Ask for an appointment for your son.
3. Bring proof that your family gets food assistance (SNAP), like an approval letter. Also ask the clinic what ID or proof of address to bring. Your son will need to come to the visit for the health check.

**Why it looks likely**
- Your son is under 5.
- Tennessee says people who show proof of food assistance (SNAP) are automatically income-eligible for WIC. If that didn't count for some reason, a family of 3 can also qualify with income up to $50,542 a year before taxes (July 2026 to June 2027).

(Source: [Tennessee Department of Health WIC page](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html))

The clinic makes the final decision, so this isn't a promise. If you have questions or need help finding a clinic, you can also call 211.

Do you want me to check whether your son might also qualify for TennCare or CoverKids (health insurance for kids)? I'd just need to know roughly your household's income before taxes and how often you're paid.
yes please check. he makes $2,500 a month before taxes. I don't work. I think he gets paid monthly but not totally sure

Your son looks **likely** to qualify for children's health coverage, either TennCare or CoverKids. Apply for him, and the state will decide which program fits.

**Why it looks likely**
- Your family of 3 has about $2,500 a month before taxes.
- A third-party site, [Talk to MIRA](https://www.talktomira.com/coverage/medicaid/tennessee/), lists the 2026 limits for a family of 3:
  - **TennCare** for a child ages 1 to 5: income up to about 142% of poverty, roughly $3,233 a month. That dollar figure is the site's estimate.
  - **CoverKids** (for kids who earn too much for TennCare): income up to about 255% of poverty, $5,806 a month.
- Your income is under both numbers.

**How sure am I?**
- Tennessee's official TennCare and CoverKids income pages wouldn't open for me. I could only check these numbers on a third-party site, so they may be a little off.
- Your income is well under both limits, so the answer probably wouldn't change.
- Check your husband's pay stub. If he's paid weekly or every two weeks, the monthly total can be different from what you expect. The state will want the exact amount.

**How to apply**
- Online: [tenncareconnect.tn.gov](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov)
- Phone: TennCare Connect, 855-259-0701. I found this number in search results but couldn't open the official page to confirm it.
- For free local help, call 211.

**Two other notes**
- You and your husband would be checked on separate, stricter income rules for adult coverage. I haven't looked at those. I can if you'd like.
- Only the state decides, and this isn't a promise. Report your income accurately on the application.

Do you want me to check whether you or your husband might qualify for TennCare too?

Sources:
- [Talk to MIRA: Tennessee Medicaid income limits for 2026](https://www.talktomira.com/coverage/medicaid/tennessee/)
yeah please check. I don't have any income, I don't work. he's the only one with a paycheck

**TennCare for you and your husband looks unlikely, but it's close. You can still apply.**

**Why**
- Tennessee covers parents with low income. The limit is about 105% of poverty for a family of 3, according to [healthinsurance.org](https://www.healthinsurance.org/medicaid/tennessee/).
- That works out to roughly **$2,330 to $2,390 a month before taxes**. I found those dollar amounts in search results, not on an official page I could open. Sources differ by a few dollars.
- Your household income is about $2,500 a month, which is a little over that line.

**Why it's worth a second look**
- The state may count income a bit differently, for example after some pre-tax deductions. That could bring you under the limit.
- I don't know if your husband's pay is exactly $2,500 a month. Check his pay stub. If he's paid weekly or every two weeks, the monthly amount may be different.
- TennCare has no savings limit for parents, so that wouldn't matter.

**If TennCare doesn't work out**
- You can apply for a health plan on HealthCare.gov or call 1-800-318-2596. Families above the TennCare parent limit may get help paying for premiums. (Source: [healthinsurance.org](https://www.healthinsurance.org/medicaid/tennessee/))
- Your son would likely still get coverage through TennCare or CoverKids, as we covered earlier.

**Next steps**
- Apply for the whole family at [tenncareconnect.tn.gov](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov) or by phone at 855-259-0701. The application will check each of you for the right program. I couldn't confirm that phone number on an official page.
- For free local help, call 211.

This is only a first look. TennCare makes the final decision, and I can't promise an outcome. Report income exactly as it is on the application.

Sources:
- [healthinsurance.org: Medicaid in Tennessee](https://www.healthinsurance.org/medicaid/tennessee/)

Tennessee WIC serves infants and children up to age five, and enrollment in SNAP can satisfy the income test automatically.

- **Age category:** The state program is described as serving income-eligible pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women, plus infants and children until their fifth birthday (The Tennessee WIC Program provides supplemental food assistance and nutrition education to income-eligible pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women, infants, and children until age five.). Caregivers such as grandparents, foster parents, and guardians can apply for a child under five in their care (Caretakers, guardians, and foster families can apply on behalf of a child under 5 who is in their care.).
- **Income limit:** Nashville's WIC program puts the cap at 185% of the Federal Poverty Level.
- **Automatic eligibility via SNAP:** Nashville says if you or your child are currently enrolled in TennCare, SNAP, or Families First, you may automatically meet WIC's income requirement. Knox County is broader, stating that if anyone in your household receives SNAP benefits, you automatically qualify for WIC. The sources differ on whether the SNAP recipient must be the applicant or child, or anyone in the household, so the local clinic should be checked.
- **Exception:** CoverKids does not automatically meet WIC's income requirement, however many families with CoverKids still qualify based on their household income.
- **Income measurement:** Nashville says WIC reviews the household's gross income (before taxes or deductions) for the 30 days before the certification appointment.

The sources are consistent that the automatic route applies to SNAP, TennCare, and Families First (TANF). The main discrepancy is whether SNAP receipt by any household member or only the applicant or child counts.

The Tennessee WIC income limit for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 is 185% of the federal poverty level, and the official figures match the USDA table.

- **Limit and scope:** The Tennessee health department states that household gross income must be equal to or less than 185% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL), and the limit is uniform statewide.
- **Official 2026-2027 figures:** The state table lists annual limits of $29,526 for one person, $40,034 for two, $50,542 for three, and $61,050 for four, with monthly figures of $2,461, $3,337, $4,212, and $5,088 respectively (WIC Income Eligibility Criteria for 2026-2027). USDA's guidance gives the same one-person figures and publishes the maximum and minimum WIC income eligibility guidelines by household size for the period of July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027.
- **Discrepancy:** A BenefitsUSA blog lists slightly different figures, such as $29,520 for one person and $61,044 for four, and a weekly four-person amount of $1,174 versus $1,175 in the state table. I'd rely on the state or USDA numbers rather than that blog.
- **Automatic eligibility:** A legal-information site says that if you already receive TennCare, SNAP, or TANF, you skip the income check entirely. I did not verify this against an official source.

**Eligibility**
- You must be a Tennessee resident.
- You must be pregnant, postpartum, breastfeeding, an infant, or a child under five.
- Your household gross income must be at or below 185% of the Federal Poverty Level.
- You must be determined to be at nutritional or medical risk.

**Income limits (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), annual gross income:**
- 1 person: $29,526
- 2 people: $40,034
- 3 people: $50,542
- 4 people: $61,050
- Each additional person adds $10,508

**SNAP and other automatic eligibility**
Applicants are automatically income-eligible if they show proof of participation in SNAP, TANF (Families First), or Tennessee Medicaid (TennCare).

**How to apply**
Contact your local county health department or WIC clinic. You can find your clinic on the site's WIC Clinics page or through the WICShopper app. The page notes that its prescreening tool is not an application, so you must contact a clinic to apply. For Shelby County, call (901) 222-9980.

**Phone:** 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942)

**Website:** tn.gov/health/wic.html

tool_calls.result:
**Income limit:** Tennessee parents and caretaker relatives qualify for Medicaid (TennCare) with household income up to **105% of the federal poverty level**. The state raised this from 89% in 2024. The 105% figure includes a 5% income disregard, so the underlying limit is 100% FPL.

**Monthly dollar amount for a family of 3:** The page doesn't list a dollar figure. It links to a federal poverty level calculator, but the dollar amount isn't in the text. To estimate it, multiply the annual FPL for a family of three by 1.05, then divide by 12.

**Adults without children:** They generally cannot qualify for TennCare. Tennessee has not expanded Medicaid, so non-disabled adults without minor children whose income is below the poverty level fall into a "coverage gap." They are ineligible for both Medicaid and Marketplace premium subsidies. The page estimates about 95,000 Tennessee residents are affected.

**Medicaid expansion:** Tennessee has not implemented ACA Medicaid expansion. The page says it is one of ten states without expansion as of 2025. Expansion bills have been introduced in recent sessions, but none have passed.

**Marketplace options:** Tennessee uses HealthCare.gov. Parents with income above 105% FPL can apply there for Marketplace plans and may receive premium subsidies. Applicants can also call 1-800-318-2596. If HealthCare.gov determines someone is likely eligible for Medicaid, it forwards the information to TennCare. Enrollment in TennCare is available year-round.
